item.title: Hurricane Nolo Threatens Hawaii With Catastrophic Flooding
item.description: Hurricane Nolo is threatening Hawaii, a state already raked by multiple natural disasters since March that have caused hundreds of millions of dollars in damage. Related: Hurricane Watch Posted on Hawaii’s Big Island as Nolo Approaches The Big Island is under a hurricane watch, while flood and tropical storm watches are in effect for Maui, Lanai, Molokai and Kahoolawe. “This rainfall may produce catastrophic life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in steep terrain,” Eric Blake, a senior hurricane specialist at the US center, wrote in an analysis.

item.title: State Farm Says It’s Adding 3,000 More Jobs in Claims Next Year
item.description: State Farm handles nearly 11 million claims each year, or an average of more than 30,000 per day, according to the company. State Farm says it plans to increase the size of its claims workforce by 10%, or about 3,000 employees, starting in 2027. The company says the planned additions reflect the continued growth of State Farm and the evolving complexity of the claims environment, including new vehicles and technology, changing repair methods, and increasingly significant severe weather events.

item.title: Lawsuits Allege Six Flags Magic Mountain’s X2 Roller Coaster Caused Traumatic Brain Injuries
item.description: Three people who went to California’s Six Flags Magic Mountain have filed lawsuits saying they were left with traumatic brain injuries from the park’s famed X2 roller coaster that is advertised as a rite of passage for the “ultimate daredevil.” The filings are the latest against the world-famous amusement park operator and S&S Worldwide, the manufacturer of the X2 roller coaster cars. Extreme roller coaster has riders bracing for impact According to the Six Flags Magic Mountain website, the X2 roller coaster reaches a top speed of 76 mph (122 kph) and has a total length of 3,610 feet (1,100 meters). Their attorney, Gary Dordick, said the firm has been retained by more than 100 clients who suffered brain injuries after riding the X2 roller coaster within the past two years.

item.title: Southern California Edison Wants State Wildfire Liability Deal Before Legislators Depart
item.description: Electric utility Southern California Edison is urging California lawmakers to hold a special session before year-end to consider limiting utilities’ exposure to future wildfire liabilities, CEO of parent company Edison International Pedro Pizarro said this week. California lawmakers last month failed to pass a plan for how wildfire victims in the state get paid, and what investor-owned electric utilities like Southern California Edison and Pacific Gas & Electric are on the hook for when their equipment sparks the blazes. Southern California Edison grid equipment is being investigated for causing the Eaton Fire at that time, which started in the Los Angeles County foothills near Altadena.

item.title: Nearly 100% of U.S Now Covered By NOAA’s Flood Mapping Tool
item.description: NOAA’s National Weather Service announced today that Flood Inundation Mapping (FIM), a tool for predicting river flooding, has expanded from prior coverage of 60% of the country to 100%. The experimental mapping tool produces estimates of land area covered in water based on model forecast river flows and current conditions that predict where flooding impacts may occur in the following days, the NWS stated. “Inundation maps are a critical tool for assessing the impacts of flooding,” said NOAA Administrator Neil Jacobs, Ph.D.

item.title: ITI Capital Ltd enters special administration
item.description: On 25 September 2026, ITI Capital Ltd (ITI Capital) entered special administration. The special administrators are responsible for managing the affairs of the firm during the special administration process. If you have any questions about the special administration, you can contact the special administrators directly.

item.title: Interconnected systemic risks highlight need to expand ILS capacity: Swiss Re & LSE
item.description: A new joint analysis published by Swiss Re Institute and LSE has highlighted how artificial intelligence (AI) and supply chains are opening new pathways to systemic stress as risks become increasingly interconnected, which is driving a need for expanded capacity and leading them to highlight ILS as a crucial capital source. Jérôme Haegeli, Group Chief Economist and Head of Swiss Re Institute, commented: “Interconnected risks leave less room for error, while governments in many advanced economies have less room to respond. High debt and constrained policy buffers mean resilience cannot start when a crisis hits – it has to be built beforehand, by reducing critical dependencies, strengthening buffers and preserving the capacity to transfer risk.” Swiss Re and LSE’s report explained that the most consequential new development has been the growing interaction between risks across the financial system, the digital ecosystem, natural hazard risks, and the wider socio-economic environment.

item.title: Embassy’s Ambassador mutual cat bond and ILW fund hits ~$1bn AUM milestone
item.description: The Ambassador US mutual fund strategy operated by Embassy Asset Management, that allocates its capital to catastrophe bonds and private insurance-linked securities (ILS) that we believe to be largely ILW’s, has reached a new milestone with its net assets under management practically at $1 billion. The Ambassador Fund has grown steadily for Embassy Asset Management ever since the strategy was launched in September 2021 , demonstrating the appetite mutual fund investors have for the catastrophe bond and related ILS asset class. That’s a testament to the successful fundraising and distribution of this Ambassador cat bond fund strategy by Embassy Asset Management, which has stimulated consistent growth for the fund over time.

item.title: US mutual insurers strengthen financial results as underwriting performance improves: AM Best
item.description: AM Best, the global insurance credit ratings agency and provider of insurance market intelligence, says US property and casualty mutual insurers recorded a significant improvement in financial performance during 2025, despite continued competitive pressures and exposure to severe weather events. Mutual insurers increased distributions as improved underwriting performance and investment returns strengthened their financial position. AM Best said larger mutual insurers, which hold substantial policyholders’ surplus, have a significant effect on the composite’s overall results.

item.title: Miller appoints Vinnisha Chandrasegar as Associate Director, Treaty in Malaysia
item.description: Miller Insurance Services LLP, an independent specialist re/insurance broker, has announced the appointment of Vinnisha Chandrasegar as Associate Director, Treaty, at Miller Malaysia. Miller said the appointment forms part of its continued efforts to strengthen its treaty reinsurance capabilities in Malaysia and across the wider region. Chandrasegar joins the business following roles with Willis Re, Gallagher Re and GC, where she gained experience supporting clients and insurance and reinsurance markets across the region.

item.title: Data centre cyber risks are growing and underrecognised, reports S&P
item.description: S&P Global Ratings, a global provider of credit ratings, research and analysis, says cyber risks linked to data centres are increasing but remain underrecognised. In a new report titled, Data Center Cyber Risk Is Increasing And Underrecognised, S&P examines how the growing integration of operational technology (OT) and IT systems, combined with the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure, could increase the potential impact of cyber incidents. Cristina Polizu, an S&P analyst, commented: “A cyberattack at a data center, an operator, or in the sector’s complex supply chain could impact multiple tenants simultaneously, with potentially widespread financial and operational implications,” adding that “Mitigating data center cyber risks is often beyond the immediate focus of tenants’ cyber security operations, while defensive tools and systems continue to be developed.” S&P said the expansion of AI is contributing to growing demand for computing capacity.

item.title: Florida’s Private Railroad, Brightline, Files for Bankruptcy
item.description: Florida’s Brightline has filed for bankruptcy protection after years of lower-than-expected revenue left it unable to repay billions it borrowed to finance the Miami-to-Orlando private railroad. Brightline’s collapse into bankruptcy, while seen as virtually inevitable in recent months, is a setback for billionaire Fortress co-founder Wes Edens, who conceived of the railroad in 2012 with a vision of creating transformative infrastructure. “This new capital will be used to support Brightline Florida’s ongoing operations and help position it for long-term stability and success, in addition to repaying the post-petition financing,” according to Assured, which insures a majority of the existing senior tax-exempt bonds issued by the operating company, BrightLine Trains Florida LLC.

item.title: Ken Griffin Runs Into Miami Resistance Over Personal Helipad
item.description: Ken Griffin is running into opposition to his plans to build a personal heliport in Miami Beach, in a rare instance of pushback to the financier’s South Florida development spree. “It will be noisy.” The heliport is one of the first proposals from Griffin that’s run into significant public resistance since he moved his family and his financial firm, Citadel, to Miami in 2022. Other similar fights, including a battle over plans to transform a municipal marina in Miami into a refuge for superrich yachters, have been playing out elsewhere in South Florida.

item.description: A judge on Wednesday dismissed Donald Trump’s lawsuit accusing The Des Moines Register and its former pollster of misrepresenting the state of the 2024 presidential race, rejecting the president’s claim that the newspaper’s poll coverage violated Iowa’s consumer fraud law. Trump filed the lawsuit against Selzer, The Des Moines Register and the newspaper’s parent company in December 2024, accusing them of fraudulently publishing inaccurate poll results to damage him and help Democrats, saying coverage of polls is not protected speech. item.title: Choice Mutual brings life insurance quotes to ChatGPT
item.description: Choice Mutual has launched a ChatGPT app that lets users compare life and final expense insurance quotes from more than 25 companies. The app covers final expense, guaranteed acceptance and other life insurance policies, and directs users to an application when they are ready to proceed. Its responses draw on Choice Mutual’s library of articles and resources.

item.description: For years, the insurance industry has been working to reduce the friction that slows down underwriting, claims, and servicing. But multiply those minutes across hundreds of thousands of tasks, and the impact starts to become significant; across an entire underwriting or claims department, that time can add up to substantial new capacity that teams can redirect toward higher-value work. I would start with the workflow itself.” Pick a real underwriting or claims process.

item.title: Catastrophe-Bond Holders Bet Hurricane Polo Won’t Trigger Losses
item.description: Investors in a catastrophe bond targeting Mexico are betting they’ll be spared losses as Hurricane Polo looks set to avoid landfall as a dangerously destructive storm. Isacco Loconte, an insurance-linked securities specialist at asset manager Azimut Switzerland SA, said in a LinkedIn post earlier this week that there are more than 70 scenarios in which Hurricane Polo might trigger a payout of the Mexico cat bond, with potential losses ranging from 25% to 100%. “But right now, I’m not too concerned.” On Thursday, Hurricane Polo — a giant storm traveling at roughly 160 miles per hour (257.5 kilometers per hour) — drenched parts of Mexico with heavy rain.

item.title: Tesla’s Supervised Self-Driving System Often Misreads Speed Limits, Belgian Safety Group Finds
item.description: Tesla’s FSD automated-driving system frequently exceeded speed limits and attempted to overtake cyclists on streets where it’s prohibited, a road-safety advocacy group said, citing tests it conducted in Belgium. The Belgian group Johanna.be – which advocates for pedestrian and cyclist safety – tested Tesla’s system over 3 days in July, covering about 400 km (249 miles). It found that FSD often exceeded speed limits in 20 km/h and 30 km/h zones, and incorrectly displayed higher speed limits to drivers, potentially misleading them about how fast the vehicle should travel.

item.title: Twenty-four CFD firms closing in crackdown on misuse of UK authorisation
item.description: Twenty-one Contracts for Differences (CFD) firms have closed since 2025, following a FCA crackdown. The FCA has been challenging CFD firms that carry out little UK business but use their authorisation as a badge to make linked overseas companies look more trustworthy than they really are. The FCA was concerned the firms were misusing their authorised status to mislead consumers.

item.description: tech layoffs reached at least 94,046, up 16.8% from 80,486 in the same period of 2025. Interestingly, and unsurprisingly, many of the cuts came as tech companies redirected spending toward AI and restructured operations to reduce costs. He believes established tech companies are spending heavily on AI and cutting costs elsewhere, hoping to increase productivity with smaller workforces.

item.title: As cat bond loss multiples tighten, AM Best urges investors towards greater selectivity
item.description: As catastrophe bond loss multiples continued to tighten in the opening half of 2026, rating agency AM Best has emphasised that a combination of rising expected losses and softer returns could force investors to become more selective ahead of the upcoming January 1st renewals. The 144A property catastrophe bond weighted average loss multiple continued to tighten in the opening half of 2026, which as AM Best indicated in a recent report, is further evidence of abundant investor capital and investor willingness to accept a lower premium for the risk. You can analyse catastrophe bond loss multiples, by year and by quarter of issuance in our interactive charts : Moreover, AM Best’s report also highlights that the weighted average spread fell 96 basis points as weighted average expected loss drifted higher by 30 basis points compared to the cohort of cat bonds issued in the first half of 2025.

item.title: ILS capital providers well positioned to complement re/insurers’ data centre needs: Stahel, LGT
item.description: With AI-driven infrastructure growth creating high levels of demand for catastrophe capacity within the re/insurance industry, Michael Stahel of LGT ILS Partners, has called out how alternative capital providers are well positioned to complement the needs that are being imposed onto traditional insurers and reinsurers amongst this build out. Adding: “As project sizes continue to increase, alternative capital is well positioned to complement the need imposed on traditional insurers and reinsurers.” While operational risks, including technology failures, cyber incidents, and equipment obsolescence are primarily managed by specialist insurers, Stahel stressed that large data centre campuses increasingly represent multi-billion-dollar concentrations of value that are exposed to major perils such as hail, severe convective storm, tornado, earthquake and flood. The objective is to understand the risk characteristics, accumulation dynamics and capital requirements of data centre exposures, and to determine where and how we can prudently allocate capital within this growing market opportunity,” he said.

item.title: Liberty Mutual Insurance hires Sinniah as Head of Capital Solutions, Global Risk Solutions
item.description: Liberty Mutual Insurance has announced the hire of Shaun Sinniah from Miller, who joins as Head of Capital Solutions for Global Risk Solutions (GRS), effective September 28th, 2026. Liberty Mutual Insurance explained that the newly created role will support Global Risk Solutions’ strategy to strengthen connection between its risk and capital capabilities. As Head of Capital Solutions, GRS, Sinniah will primarily focus on developing new business opportunities and expanding how GRS deploys capital to create value for its customers and partners.

Jérôme Haegeli, Group Chief Economist and Head of Swiss Re Institute, stated: “Interconnected risks leave less room for error, while governments in many advanced economies have less room to respond. The research, which analysed filings from 91 Fortune-100 companies between 2019 and 2016, revealed a 24% increase in the links between risks, with AI and supply chains emerging as key points of connection.

item.title: IAG reaches settlement over A$2.8bn Credit Suisse Greensill claims
item.description: Insurance Australia Group (IAG) has reached a confidential settlement with Credit Suisse entities over approximately A$2.8bn of claims arising from the collapse of Greensill, in the latest step towards winding down a major trade credit insurance dispute. IAG said in a new update today that its subsidiary Insurance Australia Limited (IAL) had agreed to settle the Credit Suisse proceedings in the Federal Court of Australia. The aggregate face value of the claims was approximately A$2.8bn plus interest, although IAG said the settlement would have no material impact on its financial position or FY27 financial results because of anticipated recoveries under insurance and reinsurance arrangements and other indemnities.

item.title: Pacific Life Re appoints Mei Sum Chan as Head of Medical Analytics
item.description: Global life reinsurer Pacific Life Re has announced the appointment of Mei Sum Chan as Head of Medical Analytics. Pacific Life Re noted that Medical Analytics plays an important role in helping it understand emerging health and mortality trends, supporting assumption development and delivering data-driven insights for its business and clients. Sum Chan succeeds Ian Collins, who retires following more than 15 years at Pacific Life Re.

item.title: People Moves: Garcia Joins InsurBanc as President and CEO
item.description: InsurBanc , headquartered in Farmington, Connecticut, named Lou Garcia as president and CEO. Garcia brings more than 25 years of leadership experience in investment banking, alternative asset management and financial services to his new role at InsurBanc. Garcia has been a vice president at Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette, which was acquired by Credit Suisse in 2000, and a vice president at JH Whitney & Co., one of the country’s oldest private equity firms.

item.title: Insurance Australia Group Settles $2B Credit Suisse Lawsuit Over Greensill Collapse
item.description: Insurance Australia Group (IAG) said on Friday it had agreed to settle an A$2.8 billion ($1.96 billion) Credit Suisse lawsuit over losses linked to the collapse of finance firm Greensill Capital. item.title: Crypto Exchange Bitget Says Hackers Stole $352 Million
item.description: Crypto exchange Bitget reported an estimated $351.6 million in unauthorized transfers from some of its wallets and temporarily suspended withdrawals. Read more: A $320 Million Hack Exposes the Cracks in Crypto’s Plumbing Founded in 2018, Bitget is one of the leading centralized crypto exchanges globally. “The scale of the drain at around three quarters of the exchange’s User Protection Fund transcends a security lapse and makes it a crisis event.” The hackers swapped about $183 million of the stolen funds for Ether tokens, according to blockchain analytics platform Lookonchain.

item.title: Groupama expands Continuity partnership in France
item.description: Groupama has signed a multi-year agreement with Continuity to use its AI-based risk management tools across the insurer’s nine regional branches in mainland France. The partnership began as a pilot with Groupama Centre-Atlantique in 2021 and expanded to all nine branches by 2025. The new agreement formalizes the broader rollout for Groupama’s professional and corporate P&C business.

item.title: Bold Penguin rebrands around DeX AI
item.description: Bold Penguin has unveiled a new website and positioned its commercial insurance platform as the Digital Exchange, powered by DeX AI. The company says the platform can take submissions from email, PDFs, ACORD forms and other systems, turn them into structured data, match risks with markets, and support quoting and binding. The updated offering spans submission intake, market intelligence, access to admitted and E&S markets, and coverage analysis.

item.title: Allstate adds auto insurance estimates to ChatGPT
item.description: Allstate has listed an app in ChatGPT that lets users request a quick auto insurance estimate by sharing details about themselves and their vehicle. The estimate starts in ChatGPT; the remaining steps take place with Allstate. The app’s description says shoppers can then continue to Allstate to customize coverage, review their quote and purchase a policy.

item.title: Louisiana Fortified Homes Program Receives $20M Investment
item.description: Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry announced this week that Louisiana is investing an additional $20 million in Fortified homes, bringing the total amount invested in state Fortified projects this year to $100 million. Earlier this year, the Legislature passed a bill that allows $50 million in additional Katrina and Rita bond money from Louisiana Citizens Property Insurance Corporation to be added to the Department of Insurance ‘s Louisiana Fortify Homes Program (LFHP). Department of Housing and Urban Development will be transferred to the Louisiana Of fice of Community Development Restore Resilient Opportunities for Overhead Fortification (Restore RO OF ) program to strengthen residential structures and reduce long-term disaster risk.

item.title: Texas Woman Pleads Guilty to Setting House on Fire
item.description: A Wharton County, Texas woman pleaded guilty to setting a house fire in July and was sentenced to 10 years deferred adjudication, the Texas State Fire Marshall Office announced. The Wharton County Sheriff’s Office arrested Rylie Bean in February at the scene of a burglary and house fire. The SFMO investigation revealed that Bean purposely set the fire which directly led to her guilty plea.

item.title: New York Sues Polymarket, Says It Ran Illegal Gambling Operation
item.description: New York’s attorney general sued Polymarket on Thursday, escalating her battle against prediction markets, an industry that she says violates state laws against illegal gambling. Attorney General Letitia James filed her petition nearly two months after bringing a similar case against Polymarket rival Kalshi. She filed similar petitions i n April against two other prediction market operators, Coinbase Financial Markets and Gemini Titan James’ case against Polymarket is the latest effort by US states to crack down on an industry that has soared in popularity since faring better than pollsters in predicting that Republican Donald Trump would beat Democrat Kamala Harris in the 2024 presidential election.

item.title: EV Sales Are Booming in Europe With Gasoline at $10 a Gallon
item.description: After years of broadly unsuccessful efforts to wean drivers off combustion engines, sales of electric vehicles are surging in Europe thanks to the jump in fuel prices stoked by geopolitical upheaval. The U.S.-Israeli war on Iran is disrupting tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, pushing the average price of a liter of gasoline in Germany to a record €2.31 a liter (equivalent to $10 per gallon). Germany, the biggest market, led the gains with a three-quarter jump while sales in France more than doubled.

item.title: Online Insurance Marketplace Insurify Blocks Meta’s Personal AI Agent Muse
item.description: 23, the online insurance marketplace said it was cutting off a different personal AI agent. Meta’s Muse has been blocked from accessing Insurify’s comparison platform because the information the AI agent spits out “risks stripping carrier quotes of critical contextual information that consumers need to make informed insurance-buying decisions,” Insurify said. We support AI agents that make insurance shopping better, but they need to preserve the information and consumer control required to make an informed insurance decision.” The spokesperson said Insurify has no exclusive relationship with ChatGPT, and the decision to block Muse was may not be exclusive either.

item.title: Europe Energy Chief Warns of Growing Risk of Attacks on Infrastructure
item.description: Companies must prepare for successful attacks on critical power infrastructure as both physical and cyber threats continue to increase, the CEO of E.ON, Europe’s largest operator of energy grids, said on Thursday. “Attacks on our grids are increasing significantly,” Leonhard Birnbaum told an industry conference, adding that both physical and cyber attacks had increased in recent years. Birnbaum said companies should abandon the idea that they could fully shield themselves from attacks and rather focus on preparation, pointing to the fact that grid assets are high in numbers and geographically spread.

item.title: Invest in Psychological Capital to Help Employees Manage Increasing Stress
item.description: However, findings from the survey reveal that organizations can help their workers manage stress and change by investing in psychological capital. “Organizations that make the effort to invest in their employees’ psychological capital will be better positioned to succeed in challenging circumstances, rather than being overwhelmed by them.” Much like financial capital, psychological capital is a resource that employers can help their workers cultivate to become more successful and resilient.
